chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Abu al-Mi'za from al-Halabi said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who performs *zihar* with his wife, then intends to finalize the divorce upon her. He said, 'There is no expiation upon him.' I said, 'If he intends to have intercourse with her?' He said, 'He does not have intercourse with her until he expiates.' I said, 'If he does, is there something upon him?' He said, 'Yes, by Allah, he is sinful, a wrongdoer.' I said, 'Is there an expiation other than the first one upon him?' He said, 'Yes, he also frees a slave.'

key_terms.يُظَاهِرُ: performs zihar (declaring wife like mother's back)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on expiation for zihar if the husband divorces his wife before resuming marital relations?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the distinct legal consequences of *zihar* based on the husband's subsequent actions, distinguishing between the penalty for divorce versus resumption of intimacy. The scholar highlights that while divorce before consummation waives the primary expiation, intercourse without prior expiation incurs both sin (*ithm*) and an additional requirement to free a slave, reflecting the severity of violating the marital bond. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the procedural integrity of *zihar* and the necessity of expiation to restore permissibility.
